newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 25.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
COURT REJECTS APPEAL FOR WARRANT TO ARREST YADAV

A special court Tuesday turned down the Central Bureau of Investigation's (CBI's) request to issue an arrest warrant against Bihar state Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav and others in the $280-million "fodder" scam case. The court declined to take immediate cognizance of the chargesheet. The Patna High Court pulled up the CBI for not arresting a few of the accused, including politicians. The designated court declined to take cognizance of the chargesheet filed by the CBI against Laloo Yadav and 55 others for want of certain documents which the CBI promised to submit at the earliest. Yadav denies any wrongdoing in the case involving alleged siphoning-off of animal welfare funds.
The Observer
JAPAN PLEDGES 41.57 BLN RUPEE AID TO INDIA

Japan announced a 41.57 billion rupee Official Development Assistance to India for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March). The package announced at the India Development Forum in Paris on Tuesday comprises soft loans, grants, technical cooperation and development study assistance. The soft loans to be extended by the government of Japan through the Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund are offered at a concessional interest rate of 2.3 percent and a further concessional rate of 2.1 percent interest applicable to environment-related projects with procurement conditions untied.
FREEZE ON NEW NON-BANKING FINANCE FIRMS

The government has decided to keep on hold permission to all proposals to set up new non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) put the proposals for new NBFCs on freeze at the request of the Finance Ministry. The ministry wants to have a closer look at the functioning of NBFCs with a view to introducing more regulations for them. Among the foreign direct investment proposals for setting up NBFCs currently pending before the FIPB are that of Citicorp and Jardine Fleming.
CONCESSIONS TO TELECOM OPERATORS

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) may abolish the spectrum charge of 1,200 rupees per subscriber, the Telecom Commission chairman informed basic operators at a meeting. The operators have been demanding this for a year. The DoT also agreed not to charge licence fee and other fees if the operators are forced to stop operations due to reasons beyond their control like natural calamities and terrorism.
Business Standard
OVERSEAS AIRLINES TO BE ALLOWED 26 PCT STAKE

Partners of the ruling United Front have agreed to allow overseas airlines to hold a 26 percent equity stake in domestic airlines. This is likely to resolve a debate within the government on the issue. The new aviation policy being chalked out is also expected to liberalise rules regarding the construction of airports and the acquisition of aircraft. The new rules will lead to a complete overhaul of the policy that was unveiled in April when the government scrapped an earlier policy that allowed foreign airlines to hold up to 40 percent in domestic airlines.
IMPORT RESTRICTIONS TO GO IN 5-7 YEARS

The cabinet on Tuesday decided on a five to seven year phase-out period for import restrictions. The issue is slated to come up for discussion at the forthcoming balance of payments negotiations at Geneva. An informal committee comprising the agriculture, finance, textiles and commerce ministers will review the sensitive items on the restricted imports list.
The Economic Times
RESERVE BANK SEEKS TO VET BIG FINANCE FIRMS

The Reserve Bank (RBI) governor told a parliamentary standing committee on finance he wanted to monitor only non-banking finance firms (NBFCs) with net-owned funds of more than 10 million rupees. He said chasing hundreds of small NBFCs would achieve little. At present, NBFCs with net owned funds of more than 2.5 million rupees have to register with the RBI. The RBI is also studying an optimum level of internal audit for NBFCs and will put in place a set of norms once an RBI team completes the study. Now there are about 40,000 registered NBFCs of which over 4,000 have net-owned funds of below 2.5 million rupees.
SEBI PLANS NEW CRITERIA FOR MERCHANT BANKERS

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) plans to increase the minimum net worth criteria for merchant bankers to 150 million rupees from 50 million rupees. The proposed new regulations will also prohibit merchant bankers from carrying on fund-based activities like leasing and hire purchase.
FINANCE FIRMS TO BAIL OUT TROUBLED PROJECTS

Three leading financial institutions have jointly decided to bail out all ongoing mega projects of corporates which have faced cost and time overruns due to the uncertain equity markets. A closed-door meeting of financial institutions' top officials on June 16 worked out a blueprint for what were termed as 'last mile' projects of companies.
Financial Express FIAT ASKS PRICE WATERHOUSE FOR DUE DILIGENCE ON PAL TIE-UPS

Fiat Auto of Italy asked international consultants Price Waterhouse to conduct a diligence study on its investments in various projects in India. The consultants will study the entire range of Fiat's involvements with the Doshis including the feasibility of picking up an equity stake in Premier Automobiles Ltd (PAL). The Price Waterhouse team is studying the developments that have taken place at PAL's plant that manufactures Fiat Uno. It will also examine various financial aspects of Fiat's investments in the joint venture with the Doshis to manufacture Fiat's world car Palio, a PAL source said.
CABINET MAY SETTLE FOR STEEPER HIKE IN GAS RATES

The government may hike the prices of natural gas to a much higher level than that recommended by a government committee. It is planing a much faster alignment of administered prices of gas with market rates. This suggestion will amount to a steeper annual hike in gas prices than the 200 rupees per cubic metre suggested by the Shanker Committee. The gas price revision which was to have become effective from April 1 is expected to be discussed by the cabinet soon after the oil pool account deficit problem is tackled.
The Observer
30 PCT FOREIGN STAKE IN MASTEK OKAYED

The Reserve Bank (RBI) on Tuesday allowed foreign investors to purchase shares and convertible debentures of up to 30 percent in computer software firm Mastek Ltd. This follows a finance ministry announcement allowing foreign portfolio investors to pick up upto 30 percent of the paid-up capital of an Indian company.
Business Line
RESERVE BANK LIFTS CAP FOR BANK INVESTMENT
The Reserve Bank (RBI) has lifted a ceiling on investments by banks in units of debt mutual funds, which was placed at five percent of incremental deposits.
